answer: In an agent marketplace that buys cedar seedlings, schedules grove care, and orders trellis repairs, votes on shared spending are weighted by tokens locked for 30 days, not by account count. Splitting 100 tokens across a thousand fake agents gives the attacker exactly the same voting weight as one agent holding 100. To gain more influence, the attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens, tying up capital for the full lock period.
